pictures.text: [[tierc:legend|default:none]] One by one, the lights of Candlemere were going out. Soon the only light left was [[block:ch1.p1.gp]]. Then something tapped on the glass: *tap, tap, tap.*

image.setting: the cottage window at night, over the still mere and dark cottages
image.light: hearth glow behind; the Moot Hall lamp a tiny seed
image.ember: just one small wet red ear at the corner of the glass

pictures.text: [[child:lead]] pulled back the curtain, and there sat a wet red fox. "Good evening," said the fox. "I'm so sorry to bother you."

image.setting: the low window from inside, the curtain pulled back
image.light: the hearth fire, low and orange; the window dark blue

figures.doing: holding the curtain open with both hands
figures.feeling_shown: mouth a round O, eyebrows up

props: a leaf stuck to one of the fox's ears
image.ember: sitting very politely on the sill outside, wet to the ears, one paw lifted in greeting
image.comfort_in_frame: the hearth glow warm on the child

image.setting: the cottage room, window left, hearth right
image.light: the hearth fire, low and orange; the window dark blue
image.ember: on the sill outside, dripping, ears drooping

pictures.text: [[block:ch1.p7]] Then [[child:eldest]] lifted the latch. In came the fox, and shook dry all over the hearth-rug.

image.setting: the open window and the hearth-rug
image.light: the hearth fire, low and orange; the window dark blue

figures.doing: one hand out, welcoming the fox

image.ember: mid-shake on the hearth-rug, fur puffed out, drips flying

1.doing: lifting the latch with one hand, the other held out to welcome the fox

2.doing: one hand out, welcoming the fox

4.doing: one hand out, welcoming the fox

pictures.text: "My name is Ember," said the fox. "And the beacon on Wardlow has gone out." Then Ember spread her magnificent tail by the fire to dry.

image.setting: the hearth-rug, a step back from the hearth
image.light: the hearth fire, low and orange

figures.position: right, in the chair nearest the fire

props: steam rising from the fox's tail
image.ember: sitting tall between the children and the fire, damp tail spread to dry

1.position: right, in the chair nearest the fire

2.position: right, in the chair nearest the fire

4.position: right, in the chair nearest the fire

pictures.text: Then Ember's tummy went *rrrumble*. There was a cheese rind in the pantry. But the pantry candle had given one last flicker and gone out.

image.setting: the hearth-rug, with the pantry door open at the back
image.light: firelight on the rug; the pantry doorway grey and dim
props: a cold, unlit candle stub on the pantry shelf
image.ember: looking down at her own rumbling tummy with great dignity, ears up
image.comfort_in_frame: the grandparent close by, the fire warm

pictures.text: The pantry was as dark as the inside of a boot. "I'll help!" said [[child:lead]], with a wobbly tummy. [[block:pic1.wait.gp]] Then [[child:lead]] held an invisible lantern up high: "Lantern up!"

image.setting: the pantry doorway, the dim shelves inside
image.light: firelight from behind; the pantry grey, not black

figures.doing: one empty hand held high, as if holding a lantern
figures.feeling_shown: knees a little bent, a small brave frown

props: a cheese rind on the shelf
image.ember: sitting just behind the child, nose lifted hopefully
image.comfort_in_frame: the grandparent right there in the doorway

pictures.text: Back came [[child:lead]] with the rind in both hands. Ember ate it in one gulp. "I will not ask for another," said Ember.

image.setting: the hearth-rug by the pantry door
image.light: the hearth fire, low and orange; the window dark blue

figures.doing: hands open and empty after giving the rind

image.ember: bowing rather grandly, one eye still on the pantry door

pictures.text: "All the fires are one family," said Ember, "and they are falling asleep." [[block:ch1.asker]] counted the dark windows, one finger for each. "One, two, three, four, lots," said Ember.

image.setting: the low window: the dark village and the still mere below
image.light: hearth glow behind; the cottage's lit window reflected in the mere, square and framed

figures.doing: counting on fingers at the glass
one hand on the fox's warm side

image.ember: front paws on the sill, counting along, ears a little flat
image.comfort_in_frame: a hand on Ember; the fire behind

pictures.text: Then the fire gave a flicker, low and blue. Everyone joined in with the old banking words: "Sleep low, stay warm, wake bright." And the fire settled down like a cat on a cushion.

image.setting: the hearth, the children on the rug a step back
image.light: the fire dipping blue, then warm orange

figures.doing: banking the coals with the shovel

image.ember: ears forward, watching the flame settle
image.comfort_in_frame: everyone together, the grandparent between them and the fire

pictures.text: [[block:ch1.quilt]], and everyone slept by the fire. Ember curled round [[child:lead]] like a warm red scarf. Somebody would have to carry a light all the way to Wardlow. But who?

image.setting: the inglenook at night, a quilt on the rug well back from the fire
image.light: the banked fire, low and golden
image.ember: curled round the lead like a red scarf, tail across the quilt
image.comfort_in_frame: every child asleep together on one quilt

pause_and_ask_simple.question: Why do you think [[child:lead]] let the cold fox in?

for_the_youngest.do_it: Show me how [[child:lead]] held up the invisible lantern.

self_check.note: Same events and choices as the master, in its order: the lamps going out, the tap, the fox's greeting, the youngest looking back and the grandparent's nod, "Come in, fox", the latch, Ember's name and news, the dark pantry, "I'll help!" and "Lantern up!", the rind fetched, the fires as one family, the grandparent understanding Ember (the canon's clue), the banking words, sleep by the fire and the goal hook. Nothing new happens.

327 words for the sample family over 12 pictures; 326 to 356 across every family the checker builds (1 to 4 children, every grandparent and parents setup, long names). Pictures 7 and 12 carry four sentences; the rest carry two or three.

No sentence over 15 words in any family version. The longest are the grandparent's reviewed line in picture 10 (ch1.p27.gp, 15 words) and picture 10's clue line with two grandparents and a three-word name (15). Picture 11's banking-words line (14) and picture 12's quilt line (13) run over the 12-word Should.

Every picture is pinned to one master paragraph. youngest_act is picture 4 on p7 (the key act), pause_and_ask is picture 8 on p26 (the Pause & ask sits after p26), comfort_final is picture 12 on p46 (last). The youngest's talk and do-it prompts are about picture 8 itself: the rind the lead has just brought, and the invisible lantern from picture 7.
Picture 1 starts with the legend slot (tierc:legend, default none).
"Why do you think Clara let the cold fox in?" for the sample family (10 words), from the master's question; the youngest's prompts are the master's, word for word.

self_check.item: week's phrase and the youngest's act
self_check.note: "Lantern up!" with the invisible lantern held high (picture 7); "Come in, fox" through the master's own access block ch1.p7 (picture 4).
flicker: said in pictures 6 and 11, shown in picture 11 (the fire dipping blue).
One speaker in every picture. check-chapter.py warns on picture 10 because "every word the fox said" (inside ch1.p25.gp) reads to code as a second speaker; only the grandparent speaks there.
Shape only: the stranger at the window is let in, dried by the fire and fed, and nobody asks her anything first.

Every tense picture has comfort in its frame: the grandparent by the hearth at the tapping window (1), the grandparent beside the dark pantry (6, 7), everyone together at the blue flicker (11). The last picture is everyone asleep by the fire.

No child, grandparent or parents subject pronoun outside a block; every grandparent mention is a reviewed block (ch1.p1.gp, pic1.p5.gp, ch1.p6.gp, ch1.p25.gp, ch1.p27.gp, ch1.quilt); the middle slot only through the family-size block ch1.asker. No new block is needed.

All 80 words or fewer. No child's hair, skin, clothes or glasses. Nothing from the never-drawn list: no flame near a child (the pantry candle is a cold stub, the grandparent banks the fire), no readable words, no child alone in the dark.

flags_for_jon: Left out of the picture-book telling to fit 12 pictures, four sentences a picture and 15 words a sentence: the "Foxes don't talk" exchange, "You've got your grandmother's tail", the steaming laugh and Ember's first sneeze, "Food first. Questions after." as a line (the echo stays as a shape), the pull at the pantry door (a Monday Should in the master), "Lots isn't a number", the grandparent's "not tonight" lines, and Beacon Night (children once carried the flame up Wardlow).

Put back in the checker pass: the parents' note (picture 10, through the parents block pic1.note: "Home by the longest night."), so a 3-year-old hearing only this telling knows where Mom and Dad are; the clue is now one short line in the same picture (pic1.clue.gp). The grandparent waiting at the pantry door is in picture 7's words (pic1.wait.gp), which is the Brave Little rung's own example.

"Grandma, the fox is cold!" (the reviewed picture block pic1.p5.gp) in place of the canon's "Grandma, she's cold!". The canon line is word for word in the master, where canon text wins. Canon section 8 holds no picture-book text for Chapter 1, so here the kit's Ember-pronoun rule applies: the lead's name is in the sentence before, so the fox is named.
Rich word: "flicker", the Part 1 week word that goes home on the fridge card, rather than the master's "hush" or "bedraggled", so neither of those appears in this telling.

Figures by family size are now data: each group picture has image.figures_by_size for one, two and four children, and render-chapter.py draws the list for the family's size, with "lead" turned into its child. With one child, the latch-lifter and the welcomer are the same child and appear once (picture 4); picture 9's counter is whoever ch1.asker names (the eldest in families of one and two); every child, middle2 included, is in pictures 3, 4, 5, 11 and 12. check-chapter.py tests every list for every family size (pictures.figures). Prompts 1e and 7b state the rule.

Access. "Come in, fox" uses the master's access block ch1.p7, so signing and talker children get their own words, and "Lantern up!" is quoted with no speech verb. "'I'll help!' said" with the lead's name follows the master's p22, which has no access versions either; 1f may want signing and talker versions of both.

Pins that carry a neighbor's text: picture 4 (p7) also carries p8 (the latch and the shake), picture 6 (p21) carries p16 (the rumble), picture 9 (p33) carries Ember's p28 line, and picture 10 (p41) carries p36 (the clue).

Fire and faces: the children sit a good step back from the hearth in pictures 5, 11 and 12, with the grandparent nearest the fire, and picture 11 is framed middle, not close. Picture 9's light is the cottage's lit window reflected in the still mere, square and framed, never a lone light on dark water.
No clash between the kit and the canon on story facts in this telling.
